zh: 9. 康德主义的死胡同
en: 9. The Dead End of Kantianism

zh: 德国哲学家伊曼努尔·康德（1724—1804）标志着哲学史上一个转折点的开始。他出生于普鲁士的柯尼斯堡，并在那里度过了生命中的大部分时光。在政治上，他是一位自由主义者，受到卢梭思想的影响，并同情法国大革命——至少在革命的早期阶段是如此。对他思想产生另一重大影响的是科学，当时科学正在取得惊人的进步。康德本人也为科学做出了重要贡献，特别是在其《自然通史与天体理论》（1755 年）一书中，他提出了关于太阳系形成的星云假说，这一理论后来由拉普拉斯进一步发展，现已被普遍接受。
en: The German philosopher Immanuel Kant (1724-1804) marks the beginning of a turning point in philosophy. He was born in Königsberg, Prussia, where he spent most of his life. A liberal in politics, he was influenced by the ideas of Rousseau, and sympathised with the French Revolution, at least in the early stages. The other great influence on his thought was science, which at the time was making spectacular advances. Kant himself made an important contribution to science, particularly in his General Natural History and Theory of the Heavens (1755), where he put forward the nebular hypothesis for the formation of the solar system, a theory later developed by Laplace, and now generally accepted.

zh: 当康德开始其学术活动时，德国哲学已陷入僵局。莱布尼茨思想中那些闪耀的灵光，并未真正形成一个连贯的哲学学派。莱布尼茨去世后，克里斯蒂安·沃尔夫曾试图将其系统化，但结果只是将其庸俗化了。在沃尔夫手中，莱布尼茨对世界的深刻直觉被转化为最枯燥的形式主义。康德对这种形而上学的思辨深感反感，因为它试图通过无休止的抽象推理——而非观察自然——来解开宇宙之谜。与此同时，现实世界中正涌动着一股新思潮。自然科学发展迅猛，尤其在英国和法国。即便是在因三十年战争而进步停滞的沉寂德国，随着“启蒙运动”（德语称Aufklärung，相当于法国的“启蒙运动”）的兴起，文化也焕发了新生。康德是那个时代的真正产物。
en: When Kant began his intellectual activity, German philosophy had reached a dead end. The brilliant flashes of inspiration that characterised the thought of Leibniz did not really add up to a coherent school of philosophy. After his death, Christian Wolff tried to turn it into a system, but succeeded only in vulgarising it. In Wolff’s hands, Leibniz’s profound intuitions about the world became transformed into the most arid formalism. Kant was repelled by this metaphysical speculation, which attempted to solve the mysteries of the universe, not by looking at nature, but by endless abstract reasoning. Meanwhile, in the real world, a new spirit was stirring. The natural sciences were developing quickly, especially in Britain and France. Even in sleepy Germany, where the Thirty Years’ War had paralysed progress, there was a renewal of culture in the Aufklärung, the German equivalent of the French Enlightenment. Kant was the true child of his times.

zh: 他的最重要著作《纯粹理性批判》于1781 年首次出版，当时他已五十七岁，尽管该书随后在1787 年的第二版中进行了修订。在这部著作中，康德试图解决知识问题——这一问题曾引发哲学危机，其最鲜明的表现便是贝克莱的“主观唯心主义”和休谟的“怀疑论”。康德明确的目标是彻底终结旧的形而上学，因为：
en: His most important work, the Critique of Pure Reason, was first published in 1781 when he was fifty-seven years old, although it was subsequently revised in the second edition in 1787. In this work, Kant attempts to resolve the problem of knowledge, which had caused a crisis in philosophy, the clearest expression of which was the subjective idealism of Berkeley and the scepticism of Hume. Kant’s declared aim was to finish off the old metaphysics, which:

zh: ［它］似乎提供了一个特别适合在模拟竞赛中展示技巧或施展力量的竞技场——在这个领域中，至今尚无任何竞争者成功取得过一寸进展，至少，至今尚无任何胜利能获得持久的所有权。
en: [A]ppears to furnish an arena specially adapted for the display of skill or the exercise of strength in mock-contests – a field in which no combatant ever yet succeeded in gaining an inch of ground, in which, at least, no victory was ever yet crowned with permanent possession.

zh: 自然科学取得的巨大成就——尤其是在英国——意味着知识不能仅局限于纯粹的抽象思辨，那种凭空捏造理论的做法。康德决心与这种“形而上学”决裂，认为有必要回归根本。他决定着手解决一个棘手的问题：如何获得真正的知识。一方面，自然科学的显著进步指明了前进的方向。关于宇宙的本质以及人类在其中的地位的所有这些问题，无法通过抽象的思辨来解决，而只能依靠观察和实验。
en: The great successes of natural science, especially in Britain, meant that knowledge could not be confined to mere abstract speculation, which sucked its theories out of its thumb. Determined to break with this ‘metaphysics’, Kant decided that it was necessary to go back to fundamentals. He decided to tackle the thorny question of how true knowledge was to be obtained. On the one hand, the striking advances of natural science pointed the way forward. All those questions about the nature of the universe and man’s place in it could not be solved by abstract speculation, but only by observation and experiment.

zh: 科学任务不仅在于收集大量事实，更在于对自然的运行规律获得理性的洞察。为此，单纯的概括是远远不够的。正如康德所理解的那样，思维绝不能是被动的，而必须是主动的。他的最伟大著作的标题提及“理性”（Vernunft），并将之与单纯的“知性”（Verstand）明确区分开来，这绝非偶然。但理性的形式是否足以把握现实？康德对这些逻辑形式进行了深入的批判，并指出传统逻辑陷入了自相矛盾（二律背反）的状态。康德表明，从同一命题中可以推导出截然相反的结论。但在康德那里，这种矛盾仍未得到解决。
en: The task of the sciences is not merely to collect a heap of facts. It is to obtain a rational insight into the workings of nature. For this, mere generalisations are insufficient. Thinking must not be passive but active, as Kant understood. It is not an accident that the title of his greatest work refers to Reason (Vernunft), which he clearly distinguishes from mere Understanding (Verstand). But are the forms of reason adequate to comprehend reality? Kant subjected these logical forms to a searching criticism, and showed that the traditional logic falls into a state of contradiction (antimony). Kant showed that it was possible to derive diametrically opposite conclusions from the same propositions. But in Kant, this contradiction remains unresolved.

zh: 康德的认识论
en: KANT’S THEORY OF KNOWLEDGE

zh: 主体与客体的关系几个世纪以来一直是哲学的核心问题。为了简化问题，机械唯物主义者将全部重点放在客体（物质现实、自然）上，不给思考的主体留有任何作用，将其描绘成一个被动的容器；而唯心主义者则将全部重点放在主体（心灵、理念等）上。
en: The relation of subject-object was a central question in philosophy for centuries. To simplify things, the mechanical materialists laid all the stress on the object (material reality, nature), leaving no role for the thinking subject, which was portrayed as a passive receptacle, whereas the idealists laid all the stress on the subject (mind, the Idea, etc.).

zh: 康德探讨了“我们能知道什么”以及“我们如何知道”。这是哲学的核心问题之一——即知识论或认识论（epistemology）。我们的大部分知识都源于对现实世界的观察。从幼年起，我们就通过看、听、触摸等方式感知世界。渐渐地，我们构建起对自己所处世界的认知图景。这种知识就是感官知觉的知识。对于洛克这样的经验论者而言，除此之外别无其他。康德对此持不同意见。在认识世界时，心灵并非仅仅是一个可以被填入任何内容的空容器（洛克将其描述为“tabula rasa”——一张白板）。对康德而言，认知行为并非被动的，而是主动的。我们并非简单地罗列所见之物，而是有意识地进行选择、排序和解释。为此，心灵拥有其自身的方法和规则。当我们试图理解感官提供的信息（“感觉材料”）时，无论是有意识还是无意识，都会运用某些思维形式。
en: Kant asks what we can know, and how we can know it. This is one of the central questions of philosophy – the theory of knowledge or cognition (‘epistemology’). We derive the greater part of our knowledge from observing the real world. From an early age, we see things, we listen, we touch, and so on. Gradually, we build up a picture of the world in which we live. This kind of knowledge is the knowledge of sense-perception. For empiricists like Locke, there is no other kind. Here Kant disagrees. In getting to know the world, the mind is not merely an empty vessel, which can be filled with any content (Locke described it as a tabula rasa – a blank slate). For Kant, the act of cognition is not passive, but active. We do not simply make a list of the things we see, but consciously select, order and interpret them. For this, the mind has its own method and rules. There are forms of thought which we apply, consciously or unconsciously, when we attempt to understand the information provided by our senses (‘sense data’).

zh: 康德认为，知识分为两类。虽然大多数知识源于经验，但我们的一部分知识是先天的（源自拉丁语，意为“从一开始”），并不源于经验。在康德看来，我们只能认识感官经验中呈现给我们的内容。然而，那些引发我们感觉的“物自体”，却无法被认识。在此，康德可谓是在走钢丝。尽管他本人予以否认，但这些观点似乎与休谟和贝克莱的“主观唯心主义”颇为相似。康德在第二版中修改了部分表述，试图避免这一结论。在第一版中，他的一些表述若被解读，似乎暗示思考主体可能与其所感知到的对象是同一事物。后来，他修改了这一观点，坚持认为我们自身之外的事物确实存在，但它们向我们显现的只是现象，而非其“物自体”的真实面目。
en: Kant argues that there are two kinds of knowledge. While most knowledge is derived from experience, part of our knowledge is a priori (from the Latin meaning “from the beginning”), and not derived from experience. In Kant’s opinion, we can only know what is given to us in sense experience. However, the things-in-themselves, which cause our sensations, cannot be known. Here, Kant is skating on thin ice. Although he denied it, these views seem to be similar to the subjective idealism of Hume and Berkeley. Kant changed some of his formulations in the second edition to try to avoid this conclusion. In the first edition, some of his formulations could be read so as to imply that the thinking subject might be the same thing as the object which it perceives. Later, he changed this, insisting that things outside ourselves certainly exist, but they manifest themselves to us only in appearance, not as they are in themselves.

zh: 根据康德的观点，有些观念并非源于感官知觉。这凸显了康德哲学与洛克哲学之间的差异——洛克认为一切知识均来自感官。相比之下，康德主张某些知识是与生俱来的，例如对时空的认识。他说，如果我们撇开现象的所有物理方面，最终只剩下两样东西——时间和空间。时间、空间以及运动，是物质最普遍、最根本的属性。理解它们的唯一途径是将其与物质事物联系起来。但康德是一位唯心主义者。他坚持认为，时间和空间的概念是先天的。它们并非源于经验，而是他所说的“先天”概念。
en: According to Kant, there are some ideas which are not derived from sense-perception. This shows the difference between the philosophy of Kant and that of Locke, who held that all knowledge whatsoever came from the senses. By contrast, Kant claimed that some knowledge was inborn, for instance, the knowledge of space and time. If we make abstractions from all physical aspects of phenomena, he says, we are left with just two things – time and space. Now, time and space, together with motion, are the most general and fundamental properties of matter. The only way that it is possible to understand them is in relation to material things. But Kant was an idealist. He insisted that the notions of time and space were inborn. They did not come from experience, but were what he called a priori.

zh: 为了支持自己的观点，康德采用了一种非常奇特的推理方式。他认为，虽然无法想象没有时间的物体，但完全可以想象没有物体的时间；关于空间也是如此。事实上，空间和时间与物质密不可分，无法将它们与物质分离来理解。
en: To support his idea, Kant uses a very peculiar mode of reasoning. He maintains that, whereas it is impossible to think of objects without time, it is quite possible to think of time without objects; the same in relation to space. In point of fact, space and time are inseparable from matter, and it is impossible to conceive of them as apart from matter.

zh: 康德声称，可以想象一个空无一物的空间，但无法想象没有空间。但事实并非如此。没有物质的空间，与没有空间的物质一样，都只是空洞的抽象概念。事实上，时间、空间和运动是物质的存在方式，无法以其他方式加以理解。康德关于时间和空间是主观现象的观点，已被科学的发现所驳斥。
en: Kant states that it is possible to imagine space with nothing in it, but impossible to imagine no space. But this is not so. Space without matter is just as much an empty abstraction as matter without space. In point of fact, time, space and motion are the mode of existence of matter, and can be conceived of in no other way. Kant’s idea that time and space are subjective phenomena has been refuted by the discoveries of science.

zh: 在《反杜林论》中，恩格斯指出，先天知识这一概念本身就是错误的。所有观念最终都源于现实，甚至包括数学公理。诚然，如果我们撇开事物的所有物质属性，剩下的只有空间和时间。
en: In Anti-Dühring, Engels shows that the whole concept of a priori knowledge is false. All ideas are ultimately derived from reality, even the axioms of mathematics. It is true that, if we leave aside all the material qualities of a thing, all that is left is space and time.

zh: 然而，这些现在已成为空洞的抽象概念。它们无法独立存在，正如没有苹果、梨、橙子等，就不可能有“水果”；没有具体的人，就不可能有“人类”，以此类推。唯一的区别在于，“水果”或“人类”的概念是某种特定物质的抽象，而时间和空间则是物质的最一般特征，或者更准确地说，是一般物质的存在方式。
en: However, these are now empty abstractions. They cannot stand on their own, any more than there can be fruit, without apples, pears, oranges etc.; or humanity, without human beings, and so on. The only difference is that the idea of fruit, or humanity, are abstractions of a particular kind of matter, whereas time and space are the most general features, or, more correctly, the mode of existence, of matter in general.

zh: “物自体”
en: THE THING-IN-ITSELF

zh: 所有人类知识（认知）都是两个因素的产物——认知的主体和被认知的客体。知识的原材料由外部客体（物质世界）提供，而主体（思维的头脑）则为感官信息赋予形式和意义。康德与贝克莱不同，他承认外部世界的存在，因为若无外部世界，知识或经验便无从谈起。尽管如此，康德否认我们能够认识事物“自身”的真实面目。我们只能认识现象。他的根本错误在于没有看到现象与本质之间的关系。认为我们只能认识“现象”是错误的。当我认识到事物的属性时，我就认识到了事物本身。除此之外别无他物可知；没有“彼岸”，也没有“物自体”。
en: All human knowledge (cognition) is the product of two factors – the cognising subject and the cognised object. The raw material of knowledge is provided by the external object (the physical world), whereas the subject (the thinking mind) gives form and meaning to the information of the senses. Kant, unlike Berkeley, accepts the existence of an external world, without which there would be no possibility of knowledge, or experience. Nevertheless, Kant denies that it is possible to know things as they are ‘in themselves’. We can only know appearances. His fundamental mistake was not to see the relation between appearance and essence. It is wrong to think that we can only know ‘appearances’. When I know the property of the thing, I know the thing itself. There is nothing else to know; no ‘beyond’, no Thing-in-Itself.

zh: 事实上，历代以来人们一直坚信，认识事物的唯一途径正是通过感官所提供的材料，并借助反思对其进行分析。这，且仅此而已，便是认知的过程。在此，我们首次面对这样一种断言：我们所能看到和体验到的，与事物的“真实”本质之间存在某种差异。这是一个极其奇特的观念，与所有人类经验背道而驰。因此，它需要非常明确的论证。但事实是，康德根本没有对此进行论证。他只是以一种教条主义的方式断言了这一点，这与他最初设定的目标背道而驰。
en: Now it has been the conviction of every age that the only way of getting to know a thing was precisely by taking the material given to us by our senses, and analysing it by means of reflection. This, and nothing else, is the process of cognition. Here, for the first time, we are confronted with the assertion that there is some kind of difference between what we can see and experience and the ‘real’ nature of things. This is a most peculiar notion, and one which runs counter to all human experience. It therefore demands a very clear justification. But the fact is that Kant does not justify it at all. He merely asserts it in a dogmatic manner, which is the opposite of what he set out to do.

zh: “当我们看到这个时代采纳了这样一种绝望的信条——即我们的知识仅是主观的，而我们无法超越这种主观性——这标志着时代的病态，”黑格尔评论道。
en: “It marks the diseased state of the age”, remarks Hegel, “when we see it adopt the despairing creed that our knowledge is only subjective, and that beyond this subjective we cannot go.”

zh: 黑格尔和康德一样都是唯心主义者，但他属于客观唯心主义者，从未否认认识现实世界是可能的。这种客观唯心主义尽管存在种种缺陷，却远胜于主观唯心主义所带来的彻底混乱。因此，在我们这个时代的“病态”中，获得哲学家和科学家青睐的竟是康德而非黑格尔，也就不足为奇了，他们试图说服我们：我们其实无法断言物质世界确实存在；无法知晓“大爆炸”之前发生了什么（也不应去追问）；或者亚原子粒子的行为完全取决于我们是否在场进行观测。
en: Hegel, like Kant, was an idealist, but he was an objective idealist, who never denied that it was possible to know the real world. Such objective idealism is far superior, with all its faults, to the complete confusion which comes from subjective idealism. It is therefore not surprising that in the ‘diseased state’ of our own age, it is Kant, not Hegel, who has found most favour with philosophers and scientists, who wish to convince us that we cannot really assert that the physical world exists, or that we cannot know what happened before the ‘big bang’ (and must not ask), or that the behaviour of subatomic particles depends exclusively on whether we are present to observe them.

zh: 对此，我们完全赞同黑格尔的观点，正如他所言：
en: Against this, we agree a hundred times with Hegel when he says that:

zh: ［我］们所了解的关于外在自然和内在自然的一切——简而言之，即客观世界——在其自身中与思想中的表现并无二致；而思考，就是揭示对象的真理，无论该对象是什么。哲学的任务仅仅是将世人自古以来关于思想的信念，明确地带入意识之中。因此，哲学并未提出任何新东西；而我们目前的讨论已使我们得出一个结论，该结论与人类的自然信念相一致。
en: [E]verything we know both of outward and inward nature, in one word, the objective world, is in its own self the same as it is in thought, and that to think is to bring out the truth of our object, be it what it may. The business of philosophy is only to bring into explicit consciousness what the world in all ages has believed about thought. Philosophy therefore advances nothing new; and our present discussion has led us to a conclusion which agrees with the natural belief of mankind.

zh: 显然，在任何特定时刻，我们都无法完全了解一个现象。真理如同宇宙本身一样无限。但整个人类思想史的特点，正是从无知向知识的不断迈进。今天我们所不知道的，明天终将发现。因此，将“未知”与“不可知”混为一谈是一个严重的错误。康德的“物自体”仅仅是指出我们当前局限的一种方式。它并非一个谜团，而是一个待解决的问题。今天作为“物自体”的存在，明天将成为“为我之物”。这正是整个思想史——尤其是科学史——所传达的信息。
en: Evidently, at any given moment in time, we cannot know everything about a phenomenon. Truth is as infinite as the universe itself. But the entire history of human thought is characterised by a constant movement from ignorance to knowledge. What we do not know today, we will discover tomorrow. Therefore, it is a serious mistake to confuse what is not known with what cannot be known. Kant’s Thing-in-Itself is merely a way of indicating our present limitations. It is not a mystery, but a problem to be solved. What is today a Thing-in-Itself will tomorrow be a Thing-for-Us. This is the message of the whole history of thought in general, and science in particular.

zh: 实际上，“物自体”是一个空洞的抽象概念。如果我们将一个对象中所有可知的属性都剔除掉，最终剩下的将是一无所有。正如J. N. 芬德利（J. N. Findlay）呼应黑格尔的观点所正确指出的：“物自体——康德认为‘不可知’的这一概念本身，实际上却是所有抽象概念中最能被完全认识的；它是当我们刻意剔除所有经验内容以及范畴结构的任何痕迹时所得到的。”
“未知”与“不可知”之间存在着根本区别。康德在此滑向了不可知论——这种无力的学说宣称，有些事物无法被认识，因此有些问题无法被提出。芬德利得出的结论虽严厉却不失公允：“简而言之，康德始终处于一种永久的哲学迷雾之中，既不知道自己身在何处，也不知道自己将去向何方。”
“不可知之物自体”这一概念无疑是康德哲学中最薄弱的部分，而正因如此，它实际上也是现代哲学家和科学家所继承的唯一部分。
en: In reality, the Thing-in-Itself is an empty abstraction. If we take away all the properties of an object which are knowable, we are left with precisely nothing. As J. N. Findlay, echoing Hegel, correctly observes: “The Thing-in-itself which Kant holds to be unknowable is really the most completely knowable of abstractions; it is what we get when we deliberately leave out all empirical content and every vestige of categorical structure.”

There is a fundamental difference between what is not known and what is unknowable. Kant here slides into agnosticism, the impotent doctrine that says that there are certain things which cannot be known, and therefore, that there are certain questions which cannot be asked. Findlay is harsh but not unjust when he concludes that “Kant, in short, is in a permanent philosophical muddle, and never knows where he has got to nor where he is going.”

The notion of the unknowable Thing-in-Itself is undoubtedly the weakest part of Kant’s philosophy, and for that very reason is practically the only bit which has been taken over by the modern philosophers and scientists.

zh: 康德错误的根源在于将现象与本质视为互不相容的两者。思想本应被视为连接思维主体与世界的桥梁，却被视作一道屏障，横亘于主体与客体之间。康德将思想视为我们用来理解世界的工具。正如黑格尔所解释的，这种表述是令人不满意的：
en: The source of Kant’s error was to regard appearance and essence as two mutually exclusive things. Thought, instead of being seen as a bridge uniting the thinking subject with the world, is conceived of as a barrier, something standing between the subject and the object. Kant conceives of thought as an instrument which we use to understand the world. This is an unsatisfactory formulation, as Hegel explains:

zh: “批判哲学”（即康德哲学——AW）的一条主要论证脉络要求我们在探究上帝或事物的真实存在之前先暂停脚步，并告诫我们首先应审视认知能力，以确认它是否足以胜任此类努力。康德说，在着手进行需要使用该工具的工作之前，我们应当先熟悉该工具；因为如果工具不够完善，我们所有的努力都将白费。这一建议貌似合理，因而赢得了普遍的认同和赞赏；其结果是使认知从对客体的关注及对客体研究的沉迷中抽身，转而回溯自身；从而将其转向形式的问题。
en: A main line of argument in the Critical [i.e., Kantian – AW] Philosophy bids us pause before proceeding to inquire into God or into the true being of things, and tells us first of all to examine the faculty of cognition and see whether it is equal to such an effort. We ought, says Kant, to become acquainted with the instrument, before we undertake the work for which it is to be employed; for if the instrument be insufficient, all our trouble will be spent in vain. The plausibility of this suggestion has won for it general assent and admiration; the result of which has been to withdraw cognition from an interest in its objects and absorption in the study of them, and to direct it back upon itself; and so turn it to a question of form.

zh: 黑格尔指出，思想并非一种“工具”，不像在开始工作前可以先加以检验的器具。我们将面临这样一个悖论：即“工具”必须自我检验，因为思想只能通过思考来检验。在尚未知晓之前就试图去知晓，就像一个人拒绝在学会游泳之前下水一样。早在逻辑学被构想出来之前，人类就已经在思考了。事实上，包括逻辑在内的各种思维形式，都是人类在精神和实践方面长期发展的产物。物质世界中的对象通过感官知觉直接呈现在我们面前。但事情并不止于此。知性会对感官提供的信息进行加工，将其分析并分解为各个部分。这在哲学中被称为“中介”。
en: Hegel points out that thought is not an ‘instrument’, like a tool which can be examined before commencing a job. We would be faced with the paradox that the ‘tool’ would have to examine itself, since thought can only be examined by thinking. To seek to know before we know is like the conduct of a man who refuses to go into the water until he has learnt how to swim. Men and women thought long before logic was ever conceived. In point of fact, the forms of thought, including logic, are the product of a very long period of human development, both mental and practical. The objects of the physical world are immediately given to us in sense-perception. But the matter does not stop there. The understanding gets to work on the information given to it by the senses. It is analysed, broken down into its parts. This is known as mediation in philosophy.

zh: 马克思的女婿、法国社会主义者保罗·拉法格，曾以极富机智的方式阐释了“物自体”理论的实际后果：
en: Marx’s son-in-law, the French socialist Paul Lafargue, very wittily explains the practical consequences of the theory of the Thing-in-Itself:

zh: 那个吃香肠、每天领一百苏的工人非常清楚：他被雇主剥削了，从猪肉获得营养；雇主是个强盗；而香肠味道鲜美，对身体有益。“绝非如此，”资产阶级的诡辩家们——无论他们叫皮罗、休谟还是康德——都会说。他的看法只是个人观点，完全是主观的；他完全可以同样有理地坚持认为，雇主是他的恩人，而香肠是由切碎的皮革制成的，因为他无法认识“物自体”。
问题本身就没提对，这正是整个问题的症结所在……为了认识一个对象，人必须首先验证自己的感官是否欺骗了他……化学家们则走得更深——他们深入研究物质，对其进行分析，将其分解为基本元素，然后进行逆向操作，再将这些元素重新组合起来。正如恩格斯所言，从人类能够利用这些元素制造出供自己使用的物品的那一刻起，他就可以断言自己认识了“物自体”。基督教的上帝，倘若他存在且创造了世界，也做不了更多的事了。
en: The workingman who eats sausage and receives a hundred sous a day knows very well that he is robbed by the employer and is nourished by pork meat, that the employer is a robber and that the sausage is pleasant to the taste and nourishing to the body. Not at all, say the bourgeois sophists, whether they are called Pyrrho, Hume or Kant. His opinion is personal, an entirely subjective opinion; he might with equal reason maintain that the employer is his benefactor and that the sausage consists of chopped leather, for he cannot know things-in-themselves.

The question is not properly put, that is the whole trouble… In order to know an object, man must first verify whether his senses deceive him or not… The chemists have gone deeper – they have penetrated into bodies, they have analysed them, decomposed them into their elements, and then performed the reverse procedure, they have recomposed them from their elements. And from the moment that man is able to produce things for his own use from these elements, he may, as Engels says, assert that he knows the things-in-themselves. The God of the Christians, if he existed and if he had created the world, could do no more.

zh: 尽管康德无疑具有非凡的天才，但他通过隐含地为人类知识设定界限，反而给哲学和科学带来了损害。所谓“不可知论”——康德哲学中本应悄无声息地销声匿迹的那一部分——恰恰是当今时代那些希望将神秘主义引入科学的人（如海森堡）所继承的康德思想。虽然康德曾尝试对逻辑形式进行批判（这是他的巨大功绩），但他表现出某种前后不一致之处，例如在接受矛盾律这一点上。这使他陷入了新的问题。
en: Despite his undoubted genius, Kant did a disservice to philosophy and science by implicitly placing a limit on human knowledge. The theory of the unknowable, that part of Kant’s philosophy which should have been allowed to quietly sink without trace, is precisely the one thing of Kant which has been taken over in our epoch by those, like Heisenberg, who wish to introduce mysticism into science. While Kant attempted a critique of the forms of logic (this was his great merit), he displayed a certain inconsistency, for example, in accepting the law of contradiction. This led him into new problems.

zh: 逻辑的形式
en: THE FORMS OF LOGIC

zh: 《纯粹理性批判》最重要的方面，是康德对逻辑的批判：
en: The most important aspect of the Critique of Pure Reason is Kant’s criticism of logic:

zh: 逻辑自古以来便沿着这一确凿的道路不断发展，这一点从以下事实便可显而易见：自亚里士多德以来，逻辑便未能更进一步，因此从表面看似乎已达到其完善。
en: That Logic has advanced in this sure course, even from the earliest times, is apparent from the fact that, since Aristotle, it has been unable to advance a step, and thus to all appearance has reached its completion.

zh: 康德探究的重要部分涉及一般思维形式的本质，特别是逻辑形式。它们从何而来？它们代表什么？它们在多大程度上反映了真理？康德提出这些问题值得称道，尽管他并未给出充分的答案，而是满足于将这个问题留给后人。这个问题实际上直指所有哲学的根本问题——思想与存在、精神与物质之间的关系。与黑格尔一样，康德对形式逻辑评价极低，认为它是一种“似是而非的技艺……使我们的一切认知都具有知性的形式”。
康德是首位将“知性”（Verstand）与“理性”（Vernunft）区分开来的人。尽管知性发挥着重要作用，但在康德看来，它是理性思维的最低形式。它接受事物本来的样子，并基于对纯粹存在事实的记录和肤浅分类。这是形式逻辑的基础，也是“常识”的基础——后者认为事物就是它们所呈现的样子。
en: An important part of Kant’s inquiry concerns the nature of thought-forms in general, and particularly the forms of logic. Where do they come from? What do they represent? How far do they reflect the truth? It was to Kant’s credit that he asked these questions, although he did not provide an adequate answer, being content to leave that to his successors. This question really goes to the heart of the fundamental question of all philosophy – the relation between thought and being, between mind and matter. Like Hegel, Kant had a very poor opinion of formal logic, a “specious art … which gives to all our cognitions the form of the understanding.”

Kant was the first one to distinguish between Understanding (Verstand) and Reason (Vernunf). Although it plays an important role, for Kant, Understanding is the lowest form of rational thinking. It takes things as they are, and bases itself on the registration and a superficial classification of the bare fact of existence. This is the basis of formal logic, and also ‘common sense’, which takes things to be just as they seem.

zh: 但思维过程并不止步于知性和直接感官经验的层面。为了迈向辩证理解，我们需要理性的介入——理性超越直接给定的内容，将其分解为构成部分，并重新组合起来。这就是辩证法的作用。在康德之前，辩证法的艺术几乎已被遗忘。它曾被视为纯粹的诡辩和谬论，即“幻象的逻辑”。康德的伟大成就在于将辩证法恢复到它在哲学中应有的地位，即作为逻辑的一种更高形式。
en: But the process of thinking does not stop at the level of understanding and immediate sense experience. In order to proceed towards a dialectical understanding we need the intervention of Reason, which goes beyond what is immediately given, breaks it down into its constituent parts, and puts it together again. This is the role of the Dialectic. Up until Kant, the art of dialectics had been virtually forgotten. It was regarded as mere trickery and sophism, the ‘logic of illusion’. It was Kant’s great achievement to restore dialectics to its rightful place in philosophy, as a higher form of logic.

zh: 康德试图将人类知识建立在坚实的基础上，他坚持认为，人类知识必须以经验为基础。然而，这还远远不够。最初，在认知过程中，我们面对的是一大堆杂乱无章的数据，其中既无逻辑线索，也无必然联系。这通常不会被视为真正的知识，更遑论科学知识了。我们期待着更多。为了理解感官提供的信息，理性必须发挥主动作用，而不能仅仅被动接受：
en: Kant attempts to put human knowledge on a sound basis, by insisting that it must be based upon experience. However, this is insufficient. Initially, in the process of cognition, we are confronted with a confused mass of data, with no logical thread or necessary connection. This would not generally be thought of as real knowledge, still less scientific knowledge. We expect something more. In order to make sense of the information provided by the senses, it is necessary for reason to be active, not merely passive:

zh: 他们［自然科学家］认识到，理性只能感知其按照自身设计所创造的事物；它绝不能像被牵着缰绳一样追随自然，而必须依据不变的法则，凭借判断原则先行一步，并迫使自然对其问题作出回应。因为那些没有预先设想的计划而进行的偶然观察，无法归纳为一条必然的规律。但这正是理性所寻求和要求的。只有理性的原则才能赋予相互吻合的现象以规律的有效性，也只有当实验由这些理性原则指导时，它才能具有真正的实用价值。理性的确必须以从自然中获取信息为目的去接近自然，但并非以学生的身份——像学生那样听从老师所讲的一切——而是以法官的身份，迫使证人回答他自己认为有必要提出的问题。
en: They [the natural scientists] learned that reason only perceives that which it produces after its own design; that it must not be content to follow, as it were, in the leading-strings of nature, but must proceed in advance with principles of judgment according to unvarying laws, and compel nature to reply to its questions. For accidental observations, made according to no preconceived plan, cannot be united under a necessary law. But it is this that reason seeks for and requires. It is only the principles of reason which can give to concordant phenomena the validity of laws, and it is only when experiment is directed by these rational principles that it can have any real utility. Reason must approach nature with the view, indeed, of receiving information from it, not, however, in the character of a pupil, who listens to all that his master chooses to tell him, but in that of a judge, who compels the witnesses to reply to those questions which he himself thinks fit to propose.

zh: 康德与亚里士多德对逻辑规律的理解存在一个重要区别。对亚里士多德而言，这些是事物的规律；而对唯心主义者康德来说，它们仅仅是思维的规律。问题的关键在于，对康德而言，例如同一律，无法在事物本身中找到，它仅仅是由意识强加于事物的。因此，对康德来说，逻辑仅仅是一种用于整理和分类事物的便捷方法，而辩证法——正如马克思主义者所见——则从现实世界中推导出其规律，并将其重新应用于现实世界。康德的这一错误观念已被带入现代逻辑学和数学领域，在那里人们常常断言：规律、定理等仅仅是出于方便而使用的形式概念，但与客观世界并无实际联系。
en: There is an important difference between the way that Kant and Aristotle understood the laws of logic. For Aristotle, these were laws of things, whereas, for the idealist Kant, they are laws of thought only. The nub of the matter is that, for Kant, the law of identity, for example, cannot be found in the objects themselves. It is merely applied to them by consciousness. Thus, for Kant, logic is only a convenient method for ordering and classifying things, whereas dialectics, as Marxists see it, derives its laws from the real world, and applies them back again. This mistaken conception of Kant has been carried over into modern logic and mathematics, where it is often asserted that laws, theorems, etc., are only formal ideas which are used for the sake of convenience, but which have no real relation to the objective world.

zh: “二律背反”
en: THE ‘ANTINOMIES’

zh: 《纯粹理性批判》中最引人入胜的部分被称为“二律背反”。在这些论述中，康德揭示了思维中存在的矛盾。因此，康德从形式逻辑的规律出发，将其应用于经验世界，进而揭示由此产生的矛盾。康德将此视为“物自体”不可知性的证明，却未能认识到这些矛盾是客观的，且存在于现象本身之中。
en: The most interesting part of the Critique of Pure Reason is known as the antinomies. In these, Kant shows the contradictions that exist in thought. Thus, starting with the laws of formal logic, and applying them to the world of experience, Kant precedes to show the contradictions which arise. Kant takes this as proof of the unknowability of the Thing-in-Itself, instead of seeing that the contradictions are objective, and present in the phenomena themselves.

zh: 这里的基本问题是：逻辑形式与现实世界之间有何关系？形式逻辑的范畴对现实世界毫无说明作用。科学的任务正是通过观察和实验来发现现实世界的规律。然而，对世界的认识图景从未完整过，因为科学不可避免地会不断发现新的领域，并不得不持续调整其理论和命题。这才是真实的进程。然而，康德得出了截然不同的结论。
en: The fundamental problem here is: how do the forms of logic relate to the real world? The categories of formal logic tell us absolutely nothing about the real world. It was the task of science to discover the laws of the real world through observation and experiment. However, the picture of the world was never complete, since science would inevitably discover new fields all the time, and would have to constantly readjust its theories and propositions. This is the real process. However, Kant drew entirely different conclusions.

zh: 直到黑格尔出现，这些矛盾的原因才得以阐明。问题源于形式逻辑本身的性质，它将对立面视为互斥的。例如，同一性的逻辑范畴预设了其对立面——差异。当我们说某物“是”时，我们以为已经确定了它的同一性。然而，它只有在与其他事物比较时才具有同一性。约翰之所以是约翰，是因为他不是彼得、保罗等。因此，同一性预设了差异，孤立来看毫无意义。一般而言，事物除非与其对立面结合起来，否则就没有意义。没有死亡，就无法理解生命。南北、左右、男女、善恶，只有在与它们的对立面相关联时才具有意义。对立面的统一是存在的根本事实。
en: Not until Hegel was the reason for these contradictions explained. The problem arises from the nature of formal logic itself, which takes opposites to be mutually exclusive. For example, the logical category of identity presupposes its opposite – difference. When we say that something is, we think we have identified it. However, it only has identity in comparison to other things. John is John, because he is not Peter, Paul, etc. Thus, identity presupposes difference, and has no meaning in isolation. In general, things have no meaning unless taken together with their opposites. Life cannot be understood without death. North and south, right and left, male and female, good and bad, can only have meaning in relation to their opposites. The unity of opposites is a fundamental fact of existence.

zh: 黑格尔后来解释说，纯粹的、未分化的“存在”等同于“无”。如果我们仅仅局限于断言某物“存在”，却不阐明其具体属性、内在矛盾、运动与变化以及多方面的关系，我们就无法真正把握关于它的真理。如果没有进一步的具体化，单纯的“存在”最终不过是一种空洞的抽象。这种特殊的矛盾（“二律背反”）只能通过理解“存在”与“非存在”并非相互排斥，而是在“生成”的过程中相互结合来解决。
en: Hegel later explained that pure, undifferentiated being is the same as nothing. If we merely confine ourselves to the assertion that a thing is, without explaining its concrete properties, internal contradictions, motion and change, and manifold relations, we do not really grasp the truth about it. Without further concretisation, simple being turns out to be an empty abstraction. This particular contradiction (“antimony”) can only be resolved by understanding that being and not being are not mutually exclusive, but are combined in the process of becoming.

zh: 同样，作为对立面的“因”与“果”也必须作为相互作用而统一起来。如果我们试图孤立某个特定的因与果，就会立即陷入矛盾，因为在给定事例之前总有无穷多的原因；事实上，每一个孤立的事实背后都蕴含着整个宇宙的历史。同样，如果我们试图将某个特定事实理解为原因，就会进入一个无尽的现象链，沿着时间追踪下去，直至无限。
en: Similarly, the polar opposites cause and effect have to be united as interaction. If we attempt to isolate a particular cause and effect, we immediately land ourselves in a contradiction, since there are always an infinite number of causes which precede the given case; in fact, behind each isolated fact is the whole history of the universe. Similarly, if we attempt to understand a particular fact as a cause, we will enter into an endless chain of phenomena, following it in time, into infinity.

zh: 如何解决这一矛盾？如果我们遵循形式逻辑的规则，解决康德二律背反的唯一方法就是否认其范畴中恰好一半的有效性，而只承认另一半。例如，中世纪经院哲学家们宣称偶然性（偶然事件）是一个纯粹的主观概念，是无知于原因所产生的产物。事实上，宇宙中的一切都是绝对确定的，从始至终都由至高存在者预先注定。同样，传统逻辑宣称同一性是绝对的，而矛盾则被严格禁止。
en: How to solve this contradiction? If we keep within the rules of formal logic, the only solution to Kant’s antinomies is to deny the validity of exactly one half of its categories, recognising only the other half. The mediaeval Schoolmen, for example, declared chance (accident) to be a purely subjective concept, a product of ignorance of the causes. Everything in the universe was absolutely determined, in fact, preordained from the beginning to the end by the Supreme Being. Likewise, Identity was proclaimed to be absolute, and Contradiction rigorously prohibited by the traditional logic.

zh: 康德在论及二律背反的章节中指出，矛盾不仅是诡辩家的把戏，更是不可避免的。在二律背反中，他为两个相互对立的命题提供了两套证明，这些证明“并非单纯的诡辩——并非谬误，而是基于理性的本质……”
en: Kant points out in the section on the antinomies that contradiction is not just a trick of sophists, but is inevitable. The antinomies, where he gives two sets of proofs for two contrary propositions, are “not mere sophistries – are not fallacious, but grounded on the nature of reason…”

zh: 对于思辨而言，这或许是不幸的——但对人类的实践利益而言，这或许是幸运的——理性在最高远的期许之中，发现自己被一连串对立且相互矛盾的结论所包围，无论是出于尊严还是安全，她都无法从中退缩。她也不能对这些相互冲突的推理链视若无睹，将其视为单纯的交锋，更无法强求和平；因为在冲突的对象上，她有着深切的利害关系。她别无选择，只能自我反思这种理性分裂的根源——它是否仅仅源于一场误解。经过这样的探究，双方都不得不放弃傲慢的主张；但理性对知性和感官的主导地位，将建立在坚实的基础之上。
en: Unfortunately for speculation – but perhaps fortunately for the practical interests of humanity – reason, in the midst of her highest anticipations, finds herself hemmed in by a press of opposite and contradictory conclusions, from which neither her honour nor her safety will permit her to draw back. Nor can she regard these conflicting trains of reasoning with indifference as mere passages at arms, still less can she command peace; for in the subject of the conflict she has a deep interest. There is no other course left open to her, than to reflect with herself upon the origin of this disunion in reason – whether it may not arise from a mere misunderstanding. After such an inquiry, arrogant claims would have to be given up on both sides; but the sovereignty of reason over understanding and sense would be based upon a sure foundation.

zh: 真正的解决之道在于永无止境地深化认识：
en: The real resolution is the never-ending process of deepening knowledge:

zh: 因为它［理性］无法回答我们关于其综合条件的问题——除非给出一个必须由另一个问题来补充的答案，如此循环往复，直至无穷。根据它的逻辑，我们必须从一个既定的起点上升到一个更高的起点；每一部分都将我们引向更小的部分；每个事件之前都存在另一个作为其原因的事件；而存在的条件总是建立在其他更高层次的条件之上，既无法在某种自存之物——作为原初存在者——中找到终点，也无法在其中找到基础。
en: For it [reason] can give no answer to our question respecting the conditions of its synthesis – except such as must be supplemented by another question, and so on to infinity. According to it, we must rise from a given beginning to one still higher; every part conducts us to a still smaller one; every event is preceded by another event which is its cause; and the conditions of existence rest always upon other and still higher conditions, and find neither end nor basis in some self-subsistent thing as the primal being.

zh: 每一个答案只会引发一个新问题，如此循环往复，无穷无尽。没有最终的答案，这一过程也没有终点。因此，辩证思维是不教条的、开放式的。所谓“不可解”的问题，其解决方案由科学史以及人类思想史这一永无止境的过程所提供。解决思想中矛盾的唯一途径，是对逻辑进行彻底的革新，打破那些陈旧僵化的模式——这些模式既未能也无法忠实地反映一个运动、变化、充满生命力且充满矛盾的现实世界。黑格尔赞扬康德将“矛盾”这一概念重新引入逻辑学。
en: Every answer only gives rise to a new question, and so on ad infinitum. There are no final answers. No end to the process. Therefore, dialectical thought is undogmatic and open-ended. The solution to the supposedly ‘unsolvable’ problems is given by the never-ending process of the history of science and human thought in general. The only way of resolving the contradictions in thought was by a complete overhaul of logic, breaking down the old rigid schemas, which did not and could not faithfully reflect the reality of a moving, changing, living, contradictory world. Hegel hailed Kant for reintroducing the notion of contradiction into logic.

zh: 而提出“由知性范畴引入理性世界的矛盾是不可避免且本质的”这一观点，是近代哲学发展进程中最重要的步骤之一。
en: And to offer the idea that the contradiction introduced into the world of Reason by the categories of Understanding is inevitable and essential was one of the most important steps in the progress of Modern Philosophy.

zh: 然而，康德虽然提出了这个问题，却无力或不愿给出答案：“但由此提出的问题越重要，其解决方案就越微不足道。”
en: However, having posed the question, Kant was unable or unwilling to provide the answer: “But the more important the issue thus raised the more trivial was the solution.”

zh: 康德并未实现这场革命。但他最大的功绩在于指明了前进的方向。康德通过对旧有思维形式的彻底批判，揭示了其内在的不完善和矛盾之处，从而使哲学焕发了新的生机。《纯粹理性批判》表明，矛盾是思维中固有的。《纯粹理性批判》由此将辩证法重新引入了哲学。在此之前，辩证法一直被视为一种纯粹主观的推理方法。康德则表明，辩证法既非任意也非主观，而是一种完全有效的推理方法。
en: Kant did not achieve this revolution. But his great merit was to point the way forward. Kant gave philosophy a new lease of life, by subjecting the old forms of thought to a thorough criticism, revealing their inherently unsatisfactory and contradictory nature. The Critique of Pure Reason showed that contradictions were inherent in thinking. In so doing, Kant reintroduced dialectics into philosophy. Hitherto, dialectics was regarded as a purely subjective method of reasoning. Kant showed that dialectics was neither arbitrary nor subjective, but an entirely valid method of reasoning.

zh: 尽管在当时堪称革命性，但康德的哲学并不能被视为对其所提出的问题的满意解答。最重要的是，康德的辩证法更类似于古老的苏格拉底式讨论辩证法。这其中确实有其可取之处。在对立观念的斗争中，若能充分重视对方的论点，并以严谨的方式提出正反双方的论据，便能促使人们对相关问题有更全面的认识。然而，这种方法也存在不足之处：一种不可知论；一种“真理绝不会完全站在某一方”之类的肤浅观念，等等。
en: Revolutionary though it was for its time, Kant’s philosophy cannot be regarded as a satisfactory solution to the problems posed by it. More than anything, Kant’s dialectic resembles the old Socratic dialectic of discussion. There is some merit in this. The struggle between opposed conceptions, in which due weight is given to the arguments of the other side, and arguments are put forward for and against in a rigorous way, can lead to a general increase in awareness of the questions involved. Yet there is something unsatisfactory about it; a kind of agnosticism; the superficial idea that “the truth is never all on one side,” and so forth.

zh: 康德的二律背反只有四条。黑格尔则指出，事实上万物都包含一种“二律背反”（矛盾）：
en: Kant’s antinomies are only four in number. It was left to Hegel to point out that, in fact everything contains an “antimony” (contradiction):

zh: 二律背反的真正且积极的含义在于：每一个实际事物都包含着对立要素的共存。因此，认识——或者换言之，理解一个对象——等同于将其作为对立规定性的具体统一体加以意识。
en: That true and positive meaning of the antinomies is this: that every actual thing involves a coexistence of opposed elements. Consequently to know, or, in other words, to comprehend an object is equivalent to being conscious of it as a concrete unity of opposed determinations.

zh: 康德的功绩在于对传统逻辑形式进行了彻底的批判。他的缺陷则在于其在认识论上的主观主义立场。这正是他主要弱点——模棱两可、前后矛盾和不可知论——的根源。康德在揭露传统逻辑局限性的同时，却未能与其彻底决裂，结果使自己陷入了各种无法解决的矛盾之中，而他却未能解决这些问题。主体与客体（思想与存在）之间的关系问题，直到马克思和恩格斯才最终得到解决，他们指出，归根结底，所有哲学问题都在实践中得到解决：
en: Kant’s merit was to submit the traditional forms of logic to a thoroughgoing criticism. His defect lay in his subjectivist position on the theory of knowledge. This was the source of his main weaknesses – ambiguity, inconsistency and agnosticism. In failing to make a clean break with the traditional logic, while exposing its limitations, Kant landed himself in all kinds of insoluble contradictions, which he left unresolved. The problem of the relation between subject and object (thought and being) was only finally resolved by Marx and Engels, who pointed out that, ultimately, all the problems of philosophy are resolved in practice:

zh: 一切社会生活在本质上都是实践的。所有使理论陷入神秘主义的谜团，都在人类实践以及对这种实践的理解中找到了理性的解决之道。
en: All social life is essentially practical. All mysteries which lead theory to mysticism find their rational solution in human practice and in the comprehension of this practice.
